Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/README.md

```bash

```

### Complete Configuration Example with createMathPlugin

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/plugins/math.mdx

Full configuration example enabling single-dollar text math and custom error color. Set 'singleDollarTextMath' to true to enable $...$ syntax (default false) and 'errorColor' to '#dc2626' (default is 'var(--color-muted-foreground)').

```tsx
import { Streamdown } from 'streamdown';
import { createMathPlugin } from '@streamdown/math';
import 'katex/dist/katex.min.css';

const math = createMathPlugin({
  singleDollarTextMath: true, // Enable $...$ syntax (default: false)
  errorColor: '#dc2626',      // Custom error color (default: "var(--color-muted-foreground)")
});

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <Streamdown plugins={{ math }}>
      {markdown}
    </Streamdown>
  );
}
```

### Rust Language Example

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/code-blocks.mdx

Example Rust code block computing the sum of a vector. Demonstrates syntax highlighting for Rust.

```markdown
```rust
fn main() {
    let numbers = vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
    let sum: i32 = numbers.iter().sum();
    println!("Sum: {}", sum);
}
```
```

--------------------------------

### Configuration example (app/page.tsx)

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/animation.mdx

Pass an options object to the animated prop to customize animation behavior. This example shows all available options: animation, duration, easing, and sep. The default duration is 150ms, default easing is "ease", and default sep is "word".

```tsx
import { Streamdown } from "streamdown";
import "streamdown/styles.css";

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <Streamdown
      animated={{
        animation: "blurIn",  // "fadeIn" | "blurIn" | "slideUp" | custom string
        duration: 200,         // milliseconds (default: 150)
        easing: "ease-out",    // CSS timing function (default: "ease")
        sep: "word",           // "word" | "char" (default: "word")
      }}
      isAnimating={status === "streaming"}
    >
      {markdown}
    </Streamdown>
  );
}
```

--------------------------------

### URL transform example

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/configuration.mdx

Demonstrates using the urlTransform prop to proxy image URLs through a CDN. The example shows how to intercept the 'src' key and return a proxied URL, falling back to defaultUrlTransform for other cases.

```tsx
import { Streamdown, defaultUrlTransform } from 'streamdown';

// Proxy all image URLs through your CDN
<Streamdown
  urlTransform={(url, key, node) => {
    if (key === 'src') {
      return `https://your-cdn.com/proxy?url=${encodeURIComponent(url)}`;
    }
    return defaultUrlTransform(url, key, node);
  }}
>
  {markdown}
</Streamdown>
```

--------------------------------

### Python Language Example

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/code-blocks.mdx

Example Python code block generating a Fibonacci sequence. Demonstrates syntax highlighting for Python.

```markdown
```python
def fibonacci(n: int) -> list[int]:
    """Generate Fibonacci sequence up to n terms."""
    fib = [0, 1]
    for i in range(2, n):
        fib.append(fib[i-1] + fib[i-2])
    return fib

print(fibonacci(10))
```
```

### Enable caret with block style in Streamdown

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/carets.mdx

Pass the caret prop with either "block" or "circle" to enable carets. This example uses "block" and shows a typical streaming chat setup with isAnimating controlling visibility.

```tsx
import { Streamdown } from 'streamdown';

function StreamingChat() {
  const [isStreaming, setIsStreaming] = useState(true);
  const [content, setContent] = useState('');

  return (
    <Streamdown
      caret="block"
      isAnimating={isStreaming}
    >
      {content}
    </Streamdown>
  );
}
```

### Create math plugin (@streamdown/math)

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/skills/streamdown/references/api.md

Creates a math plugin with options for single-dollar text math and error color. The getStyles() method returns the path to the KaTeX CSS file. Requires importing 'katex/dist/katex.min.css'.

```tsx
import { math } from '@streamdown/math';
import { createMathPlugin } from '@streamdown/math';

const math = createMathPlugin({
  singleDollarTextMath: true, // default: false
  errorColor: '#ff0000',
});

math.getStyles(); // Returns "katex/dist/katex.min.css"
```

```tsx
import 'katex/dist/katex.min.css';
```

### Basic Static Mode Usage (app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx)

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/usage.mdx

Enable static mode by setting the `mode` prop to `"static"`. This example renders pre-generated markdown content with the code plugin. Use for blog posts or documentation where content is complete and not streaming.

```tsx
import { Streamdown } from 'streamdown';
import { code } from '@streamdown/code';

export default function BlogPost({ content }: { content: string }) {
  return (
    <Streamdown
      mode="static"
      plugins={{ code: code }}
    >
      {content}
    </Streamdown>
  );
}
```

### Run all tests with coverage and UI

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

Commands to run all tests, tests with coverage, tests with UI, and tests in watch mode from the package directory.

```bash
# Run all tests
pnpm test

# Run tests with coverage
pnpm test:coverage

# Run tests with UI
pnpm test:ui

# Run tests in watch mode (in package directory)
cd packages/streamdown
pnpm vitest
```

### Adding Context to Equations

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/plugins/math.mdx

Demonstrates how to add explanatory text around equations. The example states the Pythagorean theorem and then shows the equation with variables defined.

```markdown
The Pythagorean theorem states that for a right triangle:

$$
a^2 + b^2 = c^2
$$

where $$a$$ and $$b$$ are the legs and $$c$$ is the hypotenuse.
```

### Inline vs Block Math Example

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/plugins/math.mdx

Demonstrates the difference between inline and block math. Inline math uses single dollar signs on the same line, while block math uses double dollar signs on separate lines with newlines.

```markdown
This is inline $$E = mc^2$$ math.

$$
E = mc^2
$$

This is block math.
```

### Sequence diagram example

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/plugins/mermaid.mdx

Visualize interactions between different actors or systems using a sequenceDiagram. This example shows participants and message arrows.

```markdown
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Browser
    participant Server
    participant Database

    User->>Browser: Enter URL
    Browser->>Server: HTTP Request
    Server->>Database: Query data
    Database-->>Server: Return results
    Server-->>Browser: HTTP Response
    Browser-->>User: Display page
```
```

### Entity relationship diagram example

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/plugins/mermaid.mdx

Model database relationships using erDiagram. This example defines USER, POST, and COMMENT entities with attributes and relationships.

```markdown
```mermaid
erDiagram
    USER ||--o{ POST : creates
    USER {
        int id PK
        string email
        string name
    }
    POST {
        int id PK
        int userId FK
        string title
        text content
    }
    POST ||--o{ COMMENT : has
    COMMENT {
        int id PK
        int postId FK
        string content
    }
```
```

--------------------------------

### Using Block Math for Complex Expressions

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/plugins/math.mdx

Shows when to use block math instead of inline math for complex expressions. The example contrasts a simple slope formula with a complex integral, recommending block display for the latter.

```markdown
✅ Good: The slope is $$m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$$

❌ Avoid: $$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2} \, dx = \sqrt{\pi}$$ in the middle of text

✅ Better:

$$
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2} \, dx = \sqrt{\pi}
$$
```

```

### Focused Diagrams: User Authentication and Data Fetching

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/plugins/mermaid.mdx

Shows the recommended practice of breaking complex diagrams into smaller, focused ones. The example includes two separate Mermaid flowcharts: one for user authentication and one for data fetching, each with a descriptive heading.

```markdown
✅ Good: Multiple small diagrams

## User Authentication Flow

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Login] --> B{Valid?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Dashboard]
    B -->|No| D[Error]
```

## Data Fetching Flow

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Request] --> B[API]
    B --> C[Database]
    C --> B
    B --> D[Response]
```
```

### Advanced configuration with createCjkPlugin (app/page.tsx)

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/plugins/cjk.mdx

For advanced configuration, use the createCjkPlugin function to create a plugin instance. This example shows a Next.js page component that renders markdown with the plugin.

```tsx
import { Streamdown } from "streamdown";
import { createCjkPlugin } from "@streamdown/cjk";

const cjk = createCjkPlugin();

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <Streamdown plugins={{ cjk }}>
      {markdown}
    </Streamdown>
  );
}
```

### Caret examples

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/skills/streamdown/references/features.md

Shows block and circle caret styles. Both caret prop and isAnimating must be set; caret disappears when streaming stops.

```tsx
// Block caret (▋) - terminal style
<Streamdown caret="block" isAnimating={isLoading}>{content}</Streamdown>

// Circle caret (●) - subtle style
<Streamdown caret="circle" isAnimating={isLoading}>{content}</Streamdown>
```

--------------------------------

### Single Tilde Escape Example

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/apps/website/content/docs/termination.mdx

Shows how single `~` between word characters is escaped to prevent GFM from misinterpreting it as strikethrough. For example, `20~25°C` renders as `20~25°C` instead of applying strikethrough.

```markdown
20~25°C
```

--------------------------------

### Custom components prop example

Source: https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/blob/main/skills/streamdown/references/styling.md

Override markdown elements by passing a components object to the Streamdown component. The example shows custom h1, a, and code components with Tailwind classes.

```tsx
<Streamdown
  components={{
    h1: ({ children, ...props }) => (
      <h1 className="text-4xl font-bold" {...props}>{children}</h1>
    ),
    a: ({ children, href, ...props }) => (
      <a href={href} className="text-blue-500 hover:underline" {...props}>
        {children}
      </a>
    ),
    code: ({ children, className, ...props }) => {
      const isInline = !className;
      if (isInline) {
        return <code className="bg-gray-100 rounded px-1" {...props}>{children}</code>;
      }
      return <code className={className} {...props}>{children}</code>;
    },
  }}
>
  {markdown}
</Streamdown>
```
